template: generate_three_view.sh: clean orthographic FRONT / SIDE / BACK sheet, same scale, metre dimension lines, ancient-Chinese xianxia mountain stream running low above Qingxi village, painterly realistic stylized game art, warm grey stone, aged wood, oxidised bronze, low-saturation blue-green water, dry ochre grass, damp soil, moss; no characters or extra text. Subject: <below>
A01_straight: modular upstream riverbed segment, STRAIGHT variant: a 6 m long, 7 m wide terrain tile with a narrow rocky stream channel 2.4 m wide running straight through the middle, channel bed 0.9 m below the bank tops; the water is low, only a thin 0.15 m deep flow in the centre, exposing wet pebbles, cobbles and a dark damp mud band on both sides of the flow, plus a pale dry band higher up the banks showing where the water used to reach; irregular warm-grey stone banks with embedded boulders and roots, short grass on top; both ends cut flat with an identical channel cross-section so segments join. FRONT shows the end cross-section, SIDE shows the length, BACK the other end.
A01_bend_left: modular upstream riverbed segment, GENTLE LEFT BEND variant: about 6 m long, 7 m wide terrain tile whose 2.4 m wide rocky stream channel curves gently to the left by about 25 degrees, channel bed 0.9 m below the bank tops; low thin water flow hugging the outer bank, a gravel point-bar exposed on the inner bank, dark wet mud band and pale dry high-water band on the stone banks, a leaning boulder on the outer bank; ends cut flat with the same channel cross-section as the straight segment. FRONT shows the downstream end, SIDE shows the bend in elevation, BACK the upstream end.
A01_bend_right: modular upstream riverbed segment, SHARPER RIGHT BEND variant: about 6 m long, 7 m wide terrain tile whose 2.4 m wide rocky stream channel turns more sharply to the right by about 40 degrees, channel bed 0.9 m below the bank tops; the outer bank is a taller undercut layered rock face with exposed roots, the inner bank a low sandy gravel bar, thin low water flow, dark damp mud band and pale dry band showing the old water level; ends cut flat with the same channel cross-section as the straight segment. FRONT shows the downstream end, SIDE the bend in elevation, BACK the upstream end.
A01_narrow: modular upstream riverbed segment, NARROWING variant: 6 m long, 7 m wide terrain tile where the 2.4 m wide stream channel is pinched to about 1.2 m in the middle between two large rock outcrops, forming a small gorge with faster, slightly foamy low water, then widens again to 2.4 m at both ends so it joins the other segments; channel bed 0.9 m below bank tops, stone banks with a pale dry band showing the old higher water level, moss in the shade. FRONT shows the end cross-section, SIDE the pinch in elevation, BACK the other end.
A02_side_crack: ancient stone water-diversion trough (old aqueduct sluice), variant 1 SIDE CRACK: a 3 m long, 0.7 m wide, 0.55 m tall U-shaped channel carved from warm grey stone blocks laid end to end on a low stone footing, faint carved cloud bands on the outside; one block in the middle has a jagged vertical crack and a missing fist-sized chunk on its side, a dark wet stain and a thin trickle of water spilling out of the crack onto the ground, the water level inside is low; moss and silt at the joints. The crack must be clearly visible on the FRONT view.
A02_end_break: ancient stone water-diversion trough (old aqueduct sluice), variant 2 BROKEN JOINT: a 3 m long, 0.7 m wide, 0.55 m tall U-shaped channel of warm grey stone blocks on a low stone footing; the last block has split diagonally and its outer half has slumped and tilted away, opening a wide V-shaped gap at the joint, water leaks out of the gap into a small muddy puddle below, broken stone fragments on the ground; moss and silt at the joints; the gap must be clearly visible on the SIDE view.
A03: half-buried old formation base (ancient array plinth): a round platform about 1.8 m in diameter and 0.45 m tall made of fitted grey stone segments, tilted and partly sunk into the earth on one side, an inlaid ring of oxidised green bronze with engraved trigram-like notches, the bronze ring is broken and missing a third of its length, two loose bronze fragments half in the soil, cracked stones, moss and dry grass; a ruin fragment, not a restored complete object.
A04: silt buildup block in a narrow stream: a 2.4 m wide, 2.2 m long, 0.6 m tall bar of sandy grey-brown silt and gravel with tangled twigs, dead leaves and a small branch caught in it, blocking most of the channel so water pools behind it and only a trickle passes on one side; show beside it a second smaller CLEARED state of the same spot: the silt reduced to a low 0.1 m sandy remnant along the edges with the channel open. Label nothing except FRONT / SIDE / BACK; the cleared state can be a small inset under the SIDE view.
A05: withered water grass clump growing at the dried stream edge: a 0.9 m wide, 0.7 m tall tuft of narrow sedge blades, mostly dry ochre and straw yellow with brown tips, some blades bent and broken, a few still faintly green at the base, roots in cracked dry mud; clearly different from tall green reeds with feathery heads - this is a low drooping thirsty clump.
A06: wet mossy marker stone at the stream edge: a 1.2 m tall, 1.0 m wide upright boulder of warm grey stone; its lower part is dark and wet with a sharp line at 0.35 m (current water level), above it a pale dry band, and higher at 0.85 m a faded dark ring of dried moss and silt stains marking the old high water level, green moss on top and on the shaded side; two clear horizontal bands so a player can see the water used to be much higher.
A01_end_source: modular upstream riverbed segment, END / SOURCE TERMINAL variant: a 4 m long, 7 m wide terrain tile whose downstream end has exactly the same cross-section as the other segments (2.4 m wide rocky channel, bed 0.9 m below bank tops, thin low flow), while the upstream end closes off: the channel climbs into a jam of large tumbled boulders and a small shallow spring pool at their foot, a thin trickle seeping out between the stones, moss and ferns in the shade, dry grass on the banks that curve round and meet behind the boulders, so the river visibly starts here and the tile can end a run. FRONT shows the open downstream end cross-section, SIDE the rise into the boulder jam, BACK the closed upstream side (banks and boulders, no channel opening).
